risk_if_not_implemented: Without Achieving Security, Compliance & Resilience Requirements, security may be bolted on rather than designed in, resulting in structural weaknesses that are costly to remediate and easy to exploit. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Business / Service Interruption (R-BC-1), Recovery Failure / Unacceptable Recovery Delay (R-OR-1), Loss of Data / Service Availability (R-IP-4), and most likely increases susceptibility to Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Hazardous / Degraded Operational Environment (MT-21).

compensating_control_1.name: Secure Baseline Configurations
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to develop, document and maintain secure baseline configurations for Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that are consistent with industry-accepted hardening standards.
compensating_control_1.justification: Secure Baseline Configurations (CFG-04) provides configuration hardening that compensates for the absence of Achieving Resilience Requirements (SEA-02.1) by eliminating unnecessary services and enforcing secure settings to reduce inherent exposure. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Secure Engineering Principles
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of industry-recognized security, compliance and resilience practices in the specification, design, development, implementation and modification of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS).
compensating_control_2.justification: Secure Engineering Principles (SEA-05) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Achieving Resilience Requirements (SEA-02.1) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
